title: Refuse the hooks merge on an unparseable host settings file instead of clobbering it
action: onboard/util.rs:55-61 returns None on any settings parse error and hooks_wiring.rs:158-183 then treats the file as absent, rewriting a host's .claude/settings.json as just {"hooks":...} — permissions/env/model silently lost; same path for .codex/hooks.json via merge_codex_hooks (~:402). Narrower variants: a non-object top-level 'hooks' key loses all hook config (:162-165); a non-array hooks.<Event> value loses that event (:169-172). Fix: a file that exists but fails to parse, a non-object hooks key, or a non-array event value must produce a typed refusal naming the file and the problem with zero writes to that file (blocked action or refused apply — follow the existing blocked_* pattern used by skills sync, see onboard/apply.rs:133-179), never a silent replace/drop. Add tests: malformed JSON file preserved byte-for-byte + refusal surfaced; non-object hooks key refused; non-array event refused. Existing green-path merge test (onboard/tests.rs:504-547) stays green.

truths: A settings file with invalid JSON survives onboard apply byte-for-byte and the refusal names the file
A non-object hooks key and a non-array event value each refuse instead of silently dropping
The existing well-formed merge test still passes
